key_big: Line up the decimal points. Then add or subtract like whole numbers.
key_sub: Write zeros in empty places (3.6 = 3.60, 5 = 5.00) so every digit has a partner. Regroup across the point when you need to, bring the point straight down, and estimate to check.
body_html:
The idea: line up the decimal points

Add and subtract decimals the same way as whole numbers, but first line up the decimal points. Then ones are under ones, tenths under tenths and hundredths under hundredths. You can only add digits that are the same place.

See it on a hundredths grid

A hundredths grid is 1 whole. One column is 0.1 and one small square is 0.01.

Write it in columns

Put the decimal points in one straight line. Then add from the right, just like whole numbers, and bring the decimal point straight down into the answer.

When a column makes 10 or more, regroup just as with whole numbers. 10 hundredths make 1 tenth, and 10 tenths make 1 one, so the 1 can cross the decimal point.

Zeros hold the empty places

A zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 3.6 = 3.60 and 5 = 5.00. Write these zeros when a place is empty, most of all when you subtract. Then every digit on the bottom has a digit above it.

Example

What is 8.2 − 3.45?

Write 8.2 as 8.20. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, so 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 1 − 4 needs a regroup, so 11 − 4 = 7. Ones: 7 − 3 = 4.

Answer: 4.75

Estimate to check

Round each number to the nearest whole number and do the easy problem. 3.6 + 2.45 is about 4 + 2 = 6, so 6.05 makes sense and 2.81 does not. You can also check a subtraction by adding back: 2.63 + 2.37 = 5.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Lining up the last digits (3.6 + 2.45 = 2.81)Line up the decimal points. Write 3.6 as 3.60
Not writing the zeros (5 − 2.37 = 3.37)Write 5 as 5.00, then regroup to subtract
Forgetting to regroup across the point (4.78 + 2.56 = 6.34)10 tenths make 1 one. Add the 1 to the ones
Taking the smaller digit from the bigger one (8.2 − 3.45 = 5.25)Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. Regroup when the top is smaller
Writing 12 tenths after the point (0.8 + 0.45 = 0.125)10 tenths make 1 whole: 0.8 + 0.45 = 1.25
Leaving out the decimal point (3.6 + 2.45 = 605)Bring the point straight down into the answer

faq.q: How do you add and subtract decimals?
faq.a: Write the numbers in columns with the decimal points lined up, fill empty places with zeros, and add or subtract from the right like whole numbers. Then bring the decimal point straight down: 3.60 + 2.45 = 6.05.

faq.q: Why do you line up the decimal points?
faq.a: Lining up the points puts ones under ones, tenths under tenths and hundredths under hundredths, so you only add digits of the same place. Lining up the last digits instead gives 3.6 + 2.45 = 2.81, which is wrong.

faq.q: How do you subtract a decimal from a whole number, like 5 − 2.37?
faq.a: Write the whole number with a decimal point and zeros: 5 = 5.00. Then regroup and subtract: 5.00 − 2.37 = 2.63. Check by adding: 2.63 + 2.37 = 5.

faq.q: What does 5.NBT.B.7 mean for adding and subtracting decimals?
faq.a: It is the Common Core standard for Grade 5: add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals to hundredths using models, place value and the link between addition and subtraction. This page covers adding and subtracting.

items.q: The grid is 1 whole. The green part is 0.2 and the yellow part is 0.56. What is 0.2 + 0.56?
items.e: Each small square is 0.01 and each column is 0.1. 0.2 = 20 hundredths and 0.56 = 56 hundredths. Together: 20 + 56 = 76 hundredths = 0.76. Do not add the digits as if they were the same place: 0.2 is 20 hundredths, not 2.

items.q: The grid is 1 whole. The green part is 0.7 and the yellow part is 0.24. What is 0.7 + 0.24?

items.q: Each grid is 1 whole. The green part is 0.8 and the yellow part is 0.45. What is 0.8 + 0.45?
items.e: 80 hundredths + 45 hundredths = 80 + 45 = 125 hundredths. 100 hundredths fill one whole grid, so the sum is 1 whole and 25 hundredths = 1.25. The sum is more than 1, so 0.125 is too small.

items.q: Each grid is 1 whole. The green part is 0.7 and the yellow part is 0.65. What is 0.65 + 0.7?
items.e: 65 hundredths + 70 hundredths = 65 + 70 = 135 hundredths. 100 hundredths fill one whole grid, so the sum is 1 whole and 35 hundredths = 1.35. The sum is more than 1, so 0.135 is too small.

items.q: Each grid is 1 whole. The green part is 0.9 and the yellow part is 0.36. What is 0.9 + 0.36?
items.e: 90 hundredths + 36 hundredths = 90 + 36 = 126 hundredths. 100 hundredths fill one whole grid, so the sum is 1 whole and 26 hundredths = 1.26. The sum is more than 1, so 0.126 is too small.

items.q: The grid is 1 whole. 0.75 is shaded. The squares with an X are taken away. What is 0.75 − 0.3?
items.e: 0.75 is 75 hundredths. Taking away 0.3 (30 hundredths) leaves 75 − 30 = 45 hundredths: the squares without an X. 0.75 − 0.3 = 0.45.

items.q: The grid is 1 whole. 0.9 is shaded. The squares with an X are taken away. What is 0.9 − 0.25?
items.e: 0.9 is 90 hundredths. Taking away 0.25 (25 hundredths) leaves 90 − 25 = 65 hundredths: the squares without an X. 0.9 − 0.25 = 0.65.

items.q: The grid is 1 whole. 0.68 is shaded. The squares with an X are taken away. What is 0.68 − 0.4?
items.e: 0.68 is 68 hundredths. Taking away 0.4 (40 hundredths) leaves 68 − 40 = 28 hundredths: the squares without an X. 0.68 − 0.4 = 0.28.

items.q: Each grid is 1 whole. 1.2 is shaded. The squares with an X are taken away. What is 1.2 − 0.45?
items.e: 1.2 is 120 hundredths. Taking away 0.45 (45 hundredths) leaves 120 − 45 = 75 hundredths: the squares without an X. 1.2 − 0.45 = 0.75.

items.q: To add 0.6 + 0.27, you can write 0.6 in hundredths. 0.6 is the same as how many hundredths?
items.e: 0.6 is 6 tenths, and each tenth is 10 hundredths, so 0.6 = 0.60 = 60 hundredths. Then 0.6 + 0.27 = 60 + 27 = 87 hundredths = 0.87.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 0.35 + ☐ = 1
items.e: 1 whole is 100 hundredths and 0.35 is 35 hundredths. 100 − 35 = 65 hundredths = 0.65. Check: 0.35 + 0.65 = 1. (0.75 is wrong: 0.35 + 0.75 = 1.1.)

items.q: What is 0.6 + 0.4?
items.e: 6 tenths + 4 tenths = 10 tenths. 10 tenths make 1 whole, so 0.6 + 0.4 = 1. Writing 0.10 forgets to regroup: 0.10 is only 1 tenth.

items.q: What is 0.9 + 0.3?
items.e: 9 tenths + 3 tenths = 12 tenths. 10 tenths make 1 whole, so 12 tenths = 1 whole and 2 tenths = 1.2. 0.12 is wrong: it puts 12 in the tenths place without regrouping.

items.q: To add 3.6 + 2.45, you write 3.6 with two decimal places. Which number is equal to 3.6?
items.e: A zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 3.6 = 3 ones and 6 tenths = 3.60. 3.06 is wrong: it moves the 6 to the hundredths place.

items.q: To find 12 + 4.75, you can write 12 with a decimal point. Which number is equal to 12?
items.e: A whole number has its decimal point after the ones digit, so 12 = 12.00. Then the 2 ones sit over the 4 ones.

items.q: Ruby lined up the last digits and got 2.81. What is the correct sum?
items.e: Line up the decimal points, not the last digits: 3.60 + 2.45. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 6 + 4 = 10, write 0 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Answer: 6.05. Estimate: 4 + 2 = 6, so 2.81 is far too small.

items.q: Leo lined up the last digits and got 2.53. What is the correct sum?
items.e: 15 is a whole number, so its point is after the 5: 15 = 15.00 (not 1.5). Line up the points: 15.00 + 2.38. Hundredths: 0 + 8 = 8. Tenths: 0 + 3 = 3. Ones: 5 + 2 = 7. Tens: bring down 1. Answer: 17.38.

items.q: To find 5 − 2.37, how should you write 5 so both numbers have hundredths?
items.e: 5 is 5 ones, and its decimal point is after the 5. Write 5.00: two zeros hold the tenths and hundredths places. Then 5.00 − 2.37 = 2.63.

items.q: Zoe found 8.2 − 3.45 = 4.75. Which addition checks her answer?
items.e: Addition undoes subtraction. Add the answer to the number taken away: 4.75 + 3.45 = 8.20 = 8.2. You get back the starting number, so her answer is right.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 5 as 5.00. Hundredths: 0 − 7 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 one: the ones become 4, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 7 = 3. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Ones: 4 − 2 = 2. Answer: 2.63. Check: 2.63 + 2.37 = 5.

items.q: What is 8.2 − 3.45?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 8.2 as 8.20. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 1 − 4 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 11 − 4 = 7. Ones: 7 − 3 = 4. Answer: 4.75. Check: 4.75 + 3.45 = 8.2.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 10 as 10.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 ten: the tens become 0, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 6 = 3. Ones: 9 − 4 = 5. Answer: 5.35. Check: 5.35 + 4.65 = 10.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 3 − 8 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 one: the ones become 5, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 13. 13 − 8 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 4 = 5. Ones: 5 − 2 = 3. Answer: 3.55. Check: 3.55 + 2.48 = 6.03.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 7 − 3 = 4. Tenths: 5 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 15 − 6 = 9. Ones: 4 − 1 = 3. Tens: bring down 8. Answer: 83.94. Check: 83.94 + 1.63 = 85.57.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 7.5 as 7.50. Hundredths: 0 − 4 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 4 = 6. Tenths: 4 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 14 − 8 = 6. Ones: bring down 6. Answer: 6.66. Check: 6.66 + 0.84 = 7.5.

items.q: What is 28 − 9.6?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 28 as 28.0. Tenths: 0 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 10 − 6 = 4. Ones: 7 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 ones: 17 − 9 = 8. Tens: bring down 1. Answer: 18.4. Check: 18.4 + 9.6 = 28.

items.q: Ava bought a book for $8.75 and a pen for $1.49. How much did she spend?
items.e: Put the two prices together: add. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 5 + 9 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 7 + 4 + 1 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 8 + 1 + 1 = 10, write 10. Answer: 10.24. Check: 10.24 − 1.49 = 8.75.

items.q: Omar paid for a $13.68 lunch with a $20 bill. How much change did he get?
items.e: Change is what is left: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 20 as 20.00. Hundredths: 0 − 8 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 ten: the tens become 1, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 8 = 2. Tenths: 9 − 6 = 3. Ones: 9 − 3 = 6. Tens: 1 − 1 = 0. Answer: 6.32. Check: 6.32 + 13.68 = 20.

items.q: A ribbon is 2.5 meters long. Eli cuts off 0.75 meters for a bow. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Take the part cut off away: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 2.5 as 2.50. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 14 − 7 = 7. Ones: bring down 1. Answer: 1.75. Check: 1.75 + 0.75 = 2.5.

items.q: In a 100-meter race, Owen ran it in 14.62 seconds and Lily ran it in 13.9 seconds. How many seconds faster was Lily?
items.e: The faster runner has the smaller time. Find the difference: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 13.9 as 13.90. Hundredths: 2 − 0 = 2. Tenths: 6 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 16 − 9 = 7. Ones: 3 − 3 = 0. Tens: 1 − 1 = 0. Answer: 0.72. Check: 0.72 + 13.9 = 14.62.

items.q: It rained 2.36 inches on Monday and 1.8 inches on Tuesday. How much did it rain on the two days?
items.e: Put the two days together: add. Line up the decimal points. Write 1.8 as 1.80. Hundredths: 6 + 0 = 6. Tenths: 3 + 8 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. Answer: 4.16. Check: 4.16 − 1.8 = 2.36.

items.q: Grace's puppy weighed 4.6 kilograms. In a month, it gained 0.85 kilograms. How much does the puppy weigh now?
items.e: The puppy got heavier: add. Line up the decimal points. Write 4.6 as 4.60. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 6 + 8 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 4 + 0 + 1 = 5. Answer: 5.45. Check: 5.45 − 0.85 = 4.6.

items.q: In the long jump, Sofia jumped 3.8 meters on her first try and 3.45 meters on her second try. How much longer was the first jump?
items.e: How much longer means find the difference: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 3.8 as 3.80. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 7 − 4 = 3. Ones: 3 − 3 = 0. Answer: 0.35. Check: 0.35 + 3.45 = 3.8.

items.q: In gymnastics, Emma scored 9.35 on the beam and 8.9 on the floor. What was her total score?
items.e: Total means add. Line up the decimal points. Write 8.9 as 8.90. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 3 + 9 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 9 + 8 + 1 = 18, write 18. Answer: 18.25. Check: 18.25 − 8.9 = 9.35.

items.q: A bottle holds 1.5 liters of water. Jack drinks 0.35 liters. How much water is left in the bottle?
items.e: Take away what he drank: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Write 1.5 as 1.50. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 − 3 = 1. Ones: bring down 1. Answer: 1.15. Check: 1.15 + 0.35 = 1.5.

items.q: A family drove 125.6 miles before lunch and 87.45 miles after lunch. How far did they drive in all?
items.e: In all means add. Line up the decimal points. Write 125.6 as 125.60. Tenths: 6 + 4 = 10, write 0 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 5 + 7 + 1 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 2 + 8 + 1 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 hundred. The other places add without regrouping. Answer: 213.05. Check: 213.05 − 87.45 = 125.6.

items.q: A normal body temperature is 98.6°F. Sam has a fever of 101.2°F. How many degrees above normal is his temperature?
items.e: How many degrees above means find the difference: subtract. Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 2 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 12 − 6 = 6. Ones: 0 − 8 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 hundred: the hundreds become 0, each 0 becomes 9, and the ones become 10. 10 − 8 = 2. Tens: 9 − 9 = 0. Answer: 2.6. Check: 2.6 + 98.6 = 101.2.

items.q: In a relay race, Mia ran the first lap in 32.48 seconds and Kai ran the second lap in 29.75 seconds. What was their total time?
items.e: Total time means add the two laps. Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 tenth. Tenths: 4 + 7 + 1 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 one. Ones: 2 + 9 + 1 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Answer: 62.23. Check: 62.23 − 29.75 = 32.48.

items.q: Nora has $25. She buys a puzzle for $8.49 and a kite for $6.75. How much money does she have left?
A swim team relay is 3.2 kilometers in all. The first swimmer swims 1.45 kilometers and the second swims 0.9 kilometers. How far does the third swimmer have to swim?
items.e: Step 1, first two swimmers: 1.45 + 0.9 = 2.35 kilometers. Step 2, the rest: 3.20 − 2.35 = 0.85 kilometers. (1.66 is wrong: it lines up the last digits, 1.45 + 0.9 = 1.54, instead of the decimal points.)

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 2.45 = 6
items.e: Use subtraction: 6 − 2.45 = 6.00 − 2.45 = 3.55. Check: 3.55 + 2.45 = 6.00 = 6. (4.45 forgets to write the zeros: 6 − 2 = 4, then brings down .45.)

items.q: What number goes in the box? 7.3 − ☐ = 4.68
Round each number to the nearest whole number. Which is the best estimate for 6.82 + 3.29?
items.e: 6.82 rounds to 7 and 3.29 rounds to 3. 7 + 3 = 10. The exact answer, 10.11, is close to 10.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest whole number. Which is the best estimate for 12.15 − 4.9?
items.e: 12.15 rounds to 12 and 4.9 rounds to 5. 12 − 5 = 7. The exact answer, 7.25, is close to 7.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest whole number. Which is the best estimate for 8.47 + 5.6?
items.e: 8.47 rounds to 8 and 5.6 rounds to 6. 8 + 6 = 14. The exact answer, 14.07, is close to 14.

items.q: Maya added 3.6 + 2.45 and got 2.81. Round each number to the nearest whole number to check. What does the estimate show?
items.e: 3.6 rounds to 4 and 2.45 rounds to 2, so the sum should be about 4 + 2 = 6. 2.81 is much smaller than 6, so it is too small. Maya lined up the last digits. The correct sum is 3.60 + 2.45 = 6.05.
